Record date: 2129-07-03
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 07/03/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Continued shortness of breath, persistent cough, and increased fatigue with lower extremity edema.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for follow-up after his recent exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and congestive heart failure. He reports some improvement in his respiratory symptoms since starting the prescribed prednisone and antibiotics; however, he continues to experience significant shortness of breath, particularly with exertion. He notes that his cough remains productive, with sputum that is still greenish and occasionally blood-tinged, although the frequency of hemoptysis has decreased. Mr. Fairfax states that he is still using his albuterol inhaler frequently, approximately 15 times a day, indicating that while there has been some improvement, he remains symptomatic.
He expresses ongoing concerns regarding his fatigue, which he attributes to both his respiratory condition and the persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. The edema has shown minimal improvement despite the initiation of furosemide, and he describes it as painful, particularly when ambulating. He has continued to experience insomnia, with anxiety persisting as a significant factor affecting his sleep quality.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, - weight gain, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + persistent shortness of breath on exertion, + productive cough with greenish and blood-tinged sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 145/85 mmHg - Heart Rate: 90 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 22 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 89% on room air
General: The patient appears in mild respiratory distress, utilizing accessory muscles during breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring, oropharynx clear.
Lungs: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally with wheezing on expiration; crackles noted in the lower lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops.
Extremities: Persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, with pitting noted, particularly in the calves.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation, with partial response to treatment. 2. Congestive heart failure, with ongoing fluid retention despite diuretic therapy. 3. Insomnia secondary to anxiety and respiratory distress, with minimal improvement.
PLAN
1. Continue oral corticosteroids (prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 more days) to further reduce airway inflammation. 2. Extend the course of antibiotics (azithromycin 500 mg daily for an additional 3 days) to ensure adequate treatment of any underlying infection. 3. Adjust nebulized albuterol treatments to every 2 hours as needed, and initiate ipratropium bromide nebulizer therapy every 6 hours to enhance bronchodilation. 4. Increase furosemide dosage to 80 mg daily, with close monitoring of electrolytes and renal function to manage fluid overload effectively. 5. Schedule a follow-up appointment in one week to reassess respiratory and cardiac status, and to evaluate the need for further adjustments in treatment. 6. Continue discussing smoking cessation resources and support. 7. Refer to a sleep specialist for ongoing insomnia management, considering a trial of pharmacotherapy if CBT-I does not yield sufficient results.
The patient was counseled on the importance of adherence to the revised treatment plan, potential side effects of medications, and the need for regular follow-up. He expressed understanding and agreement with the updated management strategy.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was stable for discharge with a follow-up appointment scheduled for 07/10/29. He was instructed to seek immediate medical attention if his symptoms worsen, particularly for any signs of respiratory distress or new cardiac symptoms.
